title: Security & Pen Test Review - Acme Bank
summary: Redwood and Acme Bank reviewed the external pen test report (RedTeam Labs). Discussion covered the single critical finding (container config leading to local privilege escalation in a private deployment), remediation steps, vulnerability triage & SLA, secure SDLC improvements (SCA, SAST, SBOM), and proposed patching cadence (monthly with emergency 48h window for critical). Next steps agreed: Redwood to send full remediation plan, Acme to provide prioritized asset list and schedule a follow-up in two weeks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-01
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Sec Eng), Daniel (Acme Head of Security), Priya (IT Ops), Miguel (AppSec), Linda (Procurement)
Artifacts referenced: pen-test-report.pdf (link), vuln-tracker.xlsx (link), redwood-security-deck.pdf (link)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, real quick intent for today is to walk through the RedTeam Labs pen test results we ran against your dedicated deployment and make sure we align on remediation, timelines, and any compliance questions -- SOC 2/ISO implications, etc. If we miss anything shout up.
02:30 - Daniel: Thanks Maya. We got the summary earlier, appreciate the quick turnaround. Big concern obviously is the critical item, can you summarize that first?
05:00 - Carlos: Yeah, sure. So the pen test identified one critical, three high, and several medium/lows. The critical is a container configuration issue observed in your private/dedicated environment - basically the container runtime allowed a bind mount pattern that could be abused for local privilege escalation under certain orchestration configs. RedTeam exploited a chain that led to privilege escalation to container host context in their lab. Important to note this was validated in our dedicated-style staging deploy; not observed in hosted multi-tenant environment during their tests.
07:10 - Miguel: So is this a Redwood platform bug or a misconfig at the deployment level?
07:45 - Carlos: It's mostly a deployment configuration combined with an older container base image that had permissive mount options. So two levers: update the base image (patched kernel libs) and enforce hardened runtime flags (no-new-privs, drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN, mount propagation restrictions). We recommended a short-term mitigation (runtime policy and extra WAF/ingress filtering) and a medium-term patch (image rebuild + platform runtime policy).
10:05 - Priya: Do you have a KB or playbook we can run? Our ops team needs checklist items - we can't take down production for long windows.
11:00 - Lena: Yes, we attached a remediation spreadsheet in the artifact - high-level steps are: 1) apply runtime flags, 2) rebuild images with patched deps (OpenSSL, glibc), 3) rotate service account keys used for orchestration, 4) tighten node-level mount policies. Short term we can add an admission controller policy to block the risky mount patterns.
13:20 - Daniel: What's the risk to data residency or S3 buckets? Did they access any credentials or metadata endpoints?
14:00 - Carlos: RedTeam showed limited metadata access in the exploit chain to get local creds on the host, which allowed them to read instance metadata in the staging environment. In our evaluation the hosted control plane has stricter IAM scoping so it wasn't exploitable there. For private deployments we'll push a mandatory instance metadata access filter and recommend using IMDSv2-style protections.
16:50 - Miguel: On remediation SLAs - for critical findings we typically expect a 48-72 hour response and mitigation timeline from vendors, high within 30 days. What does Redwood commit to?
17:20 - Maya: We're prepared to commit to an emergency response: provide mitigation steps within 24-48 hours and a patch timeline within 72 hours for criticals. For highs we aim for 30 days, mediums 60-90 depending on impact. We'll put that in writing in the remediation plan.
19:10 - Linda: From procurement side, we need to know if this changes our SOC 2 posture - do you expect new control gaps?
19:50 - Lena: Not necessarily. SOC 2 is about controls; the finding is a technical vuln but the control we map to is change/config management and patching. We'll update the control narrative and include the remediation and monitoring steps in the SOC artifact pack we share. We can include audit log entries and timeline evidence for the remediation.
22:00 - Daniel: On audit logs - what level of forensic logs do you provide? We need immutable audit trails for all admin ops.
22:40 - Carlos: We provide per-request tracing and audit logs via the Console - token-level logs, admin actions, model route changes. For private deployments we can enable long-term retention and ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding. We also support immutable append-only storage for exported logs if required.
25:00 - Priya: Good. About RBAC and SSO integration - can we scope SAML + SCIM provisioning so we can offboard quickly?
25:30 - Maya: Absolutely. We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We also do role-based access (fine-grained roles) and can map to your AD groups. We'll share the SAML metadata and the SCIM schema. Note: sometimes field names get skewed in our docs (we had a typo in the last guide where "role" was "roles"), we'll send the corrected version.
28:00 - Miguel: Vulnerability management cadence - we want to avoid surprises. Do you publish SBOMs and do SCA scans in CI?
28:35 - Lena: Yes, we generate SBOMs for images used in the deployment pipeline and run SCA on build. We also run SAST for our main repo. For customers we can provide the SBOM and SCA reports for the specific build that went to your environment. We also integrate with common ticketing (Jira) to create vuln tickets programmatically.
31:10 - Daniel: For patch cadence, what's Redwood's recommendation for production? Monthly security kernel/base image patches, but emergencies for critical CVEs?
31:40 - Carlos: Recommended cadence: monthly maintenance window for non-critical updates; we do an internal patch Tuesday process. For critical CVEs we trigger an emergency patch with a 48h mitigation window and a 7-day full patch rollout if needed. We also support staged canary rollouts to reduce blast radius.
33:05 - Priya: What's the rollback plan if a patch causes regressions?
33:35 - Carlos: We keep immutable image tags and support quick rollbacks to the previous tag; we also snapshot the KV cache and can route traffic to a fallback model variant while the patch is rolled back. We'll include exact rollback commands in the remediation doc.
35:20 - Miguel: Secure SDLC ask: can Redwood run SAST scans on customer-shared plugin code? We want to ensure any customer extensions are safe.
35:45 - Lena: We can support a vetted extension program - you submit the plugin to our security intake pipeline, we run SAST/SCA, and produce a signed attestation. For private deployments we can host a local scanner in your environment if you prefer.
37:50 - Daniel: Key management - do you support BYOK? We need HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest and envelope encryption.
38:20 - Maya: Yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSMs via our BYOK flow. For private deployments we can integrate customer HSM or a vault. We'll share the KMS integration guide and notes about key rotation.
40:00 - Miguel: Any checklist for compliance evidence collection for auditors?
40:20 - Lena: We'll provide a SOC 2 artifact pack that includes: control narratives, pen test report, remediation evidence, config baselines, audit logs, SAML metadata, and KMS configuration excerpts. We'll redact anything PII but include timestamps and identifiers for audit purposes.
42:30 - Maya: Okay quick recap - we'll send the detailed remediation plan and timelines, attach the full RedTeam Labs report, provide SAML/SCIM guides and SOC 2 artifact pack, and propose a follow-up in two weeks for status. Any other questions?
44:00 - Daniel: No, that's all for now. Thanks everyone.
44:30 - Maya: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and calendar invite.
44:50 - Meeting end.
file_notes: Transcript includes natural speech, occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache) representative of Fireflies exports. Links are referenced as artifact filenames rather than full URLs.
